Hi Suzanne — thanks for flagging this.

Short answer: Calendly should pick the visitor's browser timezone, but we've seen intermittent cases where the scheduling link falls back to the org's default (or displays the host timezone) when the visitor's browser blocks location headers or when a cached redirect occurs. Chili Piper has similar quirks when proxying through certain email clients.

Two quick options that work reliably:
1) I can send a manual calendar invite (Google/Outlook) with both times listed and the meeting timezone set to Auckland so your calendar will show it correctly.
2) If you prefer the scheduling link, try toggling the timezone selector at the bottom of the Calendly page (there's a tiny link labeled "Timezone: ..."), or open the link in an incognito window to force browser timezone detection.

I'll propose a couple of slots below in NZST/NZDT and include a direct Google Meet link in the invite if that works. Camila, cc'd, has seen this behavior with other APAC prospects — any additional notes?

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0198

Subject: RE: Quick demo — confirm timezone?

Adding a concrete workaround we've used successfully:

- When the scheduling link is ambiguous, create a manual invite in the prospect's local timezone and include the UTC offset in the event title and body (e.g., "Demo 2028-05-11 10:00 (Auckland, UTC+12 / DST check)").
- Attach a short screenshot showing the time as it appears in their calendar. That removes ambiguity for attendees in different locales.
- If we send a Calendly link as a fallback, include the three most convenient times in the body so they can compare quickly.

I attached a sample invite we've used (manual-invite.ics) and a tiny screenshot example (tz-screenshot.png). We typically book the event in the prospect's timezone and set the meeting to "show both timezones" in Google Calendar when the organizer's account supports it.

Also note: New Zealand goes into DST at different dates depending on the year — in early May you can be ±1 hour depending on current DST rules. Always good to call out "check your local DST" when sending invites around transitions.

Camila

Redwood Inference
